note: p has no puff of air, like the p in "spin". With a puff it would be ph.
ph is p with a puff of air, like the p in "pin". It is never an f sound.
t has no puff, like the t in "stop". Tone 5: a rise.
th is t with a puff of air. The nn after the vowel is not a letter n: it makes the vowel nasal.
k has no puff, like the k in "skin". ua sounds like "wa".
kh is k with a puff of air, like the k in "kin". Never the ch of Scottish "loch".
ts has no puff, like the ts in "cats". With a puff it is tsh, as in 七.
b is a voiced b. The h at the end is a glottal stop, a catch in the throat: stop the vowel short.
g is a real g, as in "go". Tone 5: a rise from low to middle.
j is a voiced sound. Bite-size Taiwanese writes it [dʑ] in phonetic notation.
oo sounds like the "aw" in "law" ([ɔ]). 好 (good) has the other o, a different vowel ([ə] in Bite-size Taiwanese's notation).
Ends in m: close your lips at the end.
Ends in n: the tongue touches behind the teeth.
ing is a single ending, close to the ing of "sing".
Final p is not released: close your lips and stop, with no puff.
tsh is ts with a puff of air. Final t is not released: the tongue stops the sound silently.
Final k is not released: the back of the tongue stops the sound.
ng here is a whole syllable with no vowel: hum it through the nose.

meaning: lion, tiger, leopard, turtle, monkey, dog, elephant, deer
note: The tone mnemonic: tones 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 2 (dog), 7, 8. There is no tone 6 in the general accent.
Tone 1, no mark: high and level.
Tone 2, acute mark (á): a high fall, not an English question rise. 九 (nine) sounds the same.
Tone 3, grave mark (à): low and falling.
Tone 4, no mark, and the word ends in -h: short and cut off, lower than tone 8.
Tone 5, circumflex (â): rising.
Tone 7, macron (ū): middle and level, lower than tone 1.
Tone 8, a short vertical line above the vowel (o̍): short and high, ending in -p -t -k or -h.
Tone 1 again: high and level, like 獅. No mark means tone 1 on an open syllable.
Tone 2: start high and fall, as in 狗.
Tone 7: middle and level, as in 象.
Tone 5: rise from low to middle, as in 猴.
Tone 7: the macron sits on the n of the syllable ng. Middle and level.
Tone 8: short and high, cut off by the -h.
Tone 3: low and falling, as in 豹.
Tone 5: a rise. The circumflex goes on the i; nn makes it nasal.
Tone 2: the acute mark goes on the u.
hué has tone 2, but before tshia it is said in tone 1 (2 → 1). The Tâi-lô still shows tone 2.
kong is tone 1 and is said in tone 7 here (1 → 7): middle and level.
tshài is tone 3 and is said in tone 2 here (3 → 2).
gû is tone 5. In the general accent it is said in tone 7 here (5 → 7); some northern speakers say tone 3.
tuā is tone 7 and is said in tone 3 here (7 → 3). The last syllable, lâng, keeps its tone.
huann is tone 1 and is said in tone 7 here (1 → 7). hí, the last syllable, keeps tone 2.
Like 公園: kong (tone 1) is said in tone 7 before kin.
hó is tone 2 and is said in tone 1 here (2 → 1).
tsá is tone 2 and is said in tone 1 here (2 → 1).
tiān is tone 7 and is said in tone 3 here (7 → 3). uē, the last syllable, keeps tone 7.
tshiùnn is tone 3 and is said in tone 2 here (3 → 2).
gû is tone 5 and is said in tone 7 here (5 → 7), as in 牛肉.
pîng is tone 5 and is said in tone 7 here (5 → 7).
Tâi is tone 5 and is said in tone 7 here (5 → 7). uân, the last syllable, keeps tone 5.
tiān is tone 7 and is said in tone 3 here (7 → 3).
ūn is tone 7 and is said in tone 3 here (7 → 3); tōng keeps tone 7.
lāu is tone 7 and is said in tone 3 here (7 → 3).
Neutral tone after --: lí is said light and short, and tshù keeps its own tone 3 (no sandhi before --).
